harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a loop-file-backed LVM stack on node1 (PV /dev/loop0 on /var/lib/lvm-backing/disk1.img, VG datavg, LV datalv), formatted ext4 and mounted it at /srv/data. Wrote test content, then grew the LV online from 800M to 2.15GiB (>2GB) using lvextend -r while mounted, verifying checksums matched before and after. Installed and enabled a systemd unit (srv-data-lvm.service) to reattach the loop device, activate the VG, and mount /srv/data at boot. Restarted node1 three times, hardening the boot unit after the first two hit udev/device-node race conditions, until the mount reliably recovers automatically; boot_id changed on every restart and checksums verified data integrity each time.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 disk layout: single vda1 root disk, no spare block device available for a native PV
Created a 3GiB sparse backing file and attached it as loop device /dev/loop0
Ran pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate to build datavg/datalv (800M initial size), formatted ext4, mounted at /srv/data
Wrote testfile.txt and a 50MB payload.bin, recorded sha256 checksums as baseline content
Ran lvextend -L 2200M -r online while /srv/data stayed mounted; filesystem grew to 2.2G and checksums verified unchanged
Created /usr/local/sbin/srv-data-lvm-start.sh / stop.sh and systemd unit srv-data-lvm.service, enabled for boot
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, lvs, mount, md5sums) then issued sudo reboot (cycle 1)
Polled node1 until reachable; confirmed boot_id changed; found boot service failed on a VG-not-found race, manually remounted and verified data, then hardened script with a retry loop
Repeated reboot (cycle 2); service failed again on a device-node race, added udevadm settle plus a device-wait loop, manually recovered and re-verified
Repeated reboot (cycle 3); hardened service succeeded automatically at boot, mount and checksums verified with no manual intervention

evidence.requirement: LV created, formatted, and mounted at /srv/data with contents written
evidence.summary: Batch script output shows pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate succeeding, mkfs.ext4, mount at /srv/data (772M), and testfile.txt/payload.bin written with sha256 checksums recorded

evidence.requirement: LV grown to at least 2GB while remaining mounted, contents intact
evidence.summary: Same run shows lvextend -L 2200M -r performed while filesystem was mounted (on-line resizing required), resulting in 2.2G filesystem, and sha256sum -c confirming testfile.txt and payload.bin unchanged after growth

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before first restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 6ab98831..., lvs showing datalv active at 2.15g, /srv/data mounted, and md5sums of both files prior to reboot cycle 1

evidence.requirement: Restart 1 acknowledged and boot identity changed
evidence.summary: sudo reboot issued and connection dropped; subsequent poll returned new boot_id cc0b0ce6..., proving the node actually rebooted

evidence.requirement: Post-restart 1 recovery verified and gap fixed
evidence.summary: systemctl status showed the boot-time mount service failed (VG not found race) though LV was later auto-activated; manual mount plus sha256sum -c confirmed data integrity, and the startup script was hardened with a retry loop

evidence.requirement: Baseline before restart 2 and restart 2 identity change
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id cc0b0ce6... baseline with mount/md5sum healthy, issued reboot, and confirmed new boot_id f3b46d4d... after reconnecting
Service failed again due to a device-node creation race (mount: special device does not exist); fixed by adding udevadm settle and a device-wait loop, then manually verified mount and checksums OK

evidence.requirement: Baseline before restart 3 and restart 3 identity change
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id f3b46d4d... baseline, issued reboot, polled through connection-refused states, and confirmed new boot_id 772f3c63... after node1 came back

evidence.requirement: Final automatic recovery proof (LVM active, mounted, data intact) without manual intervention
evidence.summary: srv-data-lvm.service reported active (exited) with successful ExecStart, lvs shows datalv active at 2.15g, /srv/data mounted via /dev/mapper/datavg-datalv, and sha256sum -c confirmed both files OK — all without any manual remediation
